 Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto apologises to S’pore & M’sia over transboundary haze, adds that it is ‘not our fault’
 Featured Latest News People Singapore 
 President Prabowo said that Indonesia did its best to combat the wildfires.
 By
 Ethan Oh 
 - 16 Nov 2026, 5:28 pm 
 Follow us on Whatsapp 
 for the latest updates

 for the latest updates 
 President Prabowo apologises over wildfire haze, Indonesia investigating 104 corporations allegedly involved in fires 
 On Sunday (15 Nov), Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto apologised to Singapore and Malaysia for the transboundary haze that has impacted their people.
 However, he also added that it was “not our fault” and that the country did their best.
 Took 4 months to control wildfires
 On 15 Nov, the leaders of the member states of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) attended the 49th ASEAN Summit in Manila.
 In the plenary session, President Prabowo said that ASEAN nations must acknowledge problems between themselves , as these issues can affect neighbouring countries.
 Source: Sekretariat Presiden on YouTube
 “For instance, I would like to apologise to my neighbouring countries, Malaysia and Singapore.”
 He stated that it took Indonesia nearly four months to control its large forest fires, during which the haze travelled to the two countries.
 “This was not our fault, not our mistake. But once again, we apologise,” President Prabowo added.
 “We have done our best.”
 Source: Sekretariat Presiden on YouTube
 104 corporations under investigation for role in wildfires
 The Indonesian President claimed that the government had mobilised 71,000 firefighters. He also said 16 personnel died fighting the fires, with many more injured.
 President Prabowo also spoke about “tough measures” taken against companies that allegedly had a role in starting or spreading the wildfires.
 Source: Salim Van Java on Wikimedia Commons
 “We have revoked 17 concessions from corporations. 26 are now under investigation. 11 corporations have already been indicted and 23 are on the list that will be indicted,” he explained.
 In total, the police are investigating 104 corporations.
 Indonesian government creating fire prevention programmes
 On behalf of the Indonesian government and people, President Prabowo apologised once again for any suffering they caused Malaysians and Singaporeans.
 Source: Sekretariat Presiden on YouTube
 He stated that his government is determined to start programmes for fire prevention over mitigation.
 He concluded his speech with a call for stronger cooperation between Indonesia and its fellow ASEAN nations.
 Haze conditions in Singapore improving in November
 Raging forest fires in Indonesia have triggered the worst haze in Singapore and Malaysia since 2019
 The issue resulted in alleged tension between the countries.
 Image courtesy of xdavestrix
 Indonesian government officials rejected the need for foreign aid to combat the forest fires and even claimed that Indonesia sends oxygen to its neighbours .
 On 24 Oct, Indonesia cut its natural gas exports to Singapore by 9%. This came shortly after a minister warned of reduced exports to countries that “disrespect” Indonesia .
 While the wildfires and haze remain an ongoing issue, conditions have noticeably improved in November.
